reviews.body_html: Received the Sauna and was relatively simple to install, easy enough for 1 person to do it. Very easy to control, heats up nicely. I did not notice a huge gash in the back panel until after I had assembled and was using the sauna - there was this draft and upon investigation found a 4 inch hole in the back, not visible from the front because the heating element and slats. I didn't notice the box was damaged as that side was on the ground. Still waiting for some resolution to what Peak is going to do about it. In the meantime i put some 3M heat tape over the opening and continue to use the sauna. Red light therapy is nice but is operated via a separate application on your phone but works nicely. reviews.body_html:
I've been using my Peak Fugi Sauna for a couple months now and the experience and results have been excellent. I'm retired and very active mainly with regular pickleball play and even with a stretching routine every day, was experiencing typical aches and pains. I decided to investigate if an infrared sauna would be beneficial and which one offered the best value.

I didn't know much about the infrared sauna, so I developed a typical buyer compare matrix with the different sauna companies. I learned about and evaluated the various compare items (FIR-MIR-NIR source and wavelength, emissivity, red light therapy, wood type, warranty, service, price, delivery, etc. and the Peak product came out ahead mainly on the price-value equation where the technical features were comparable to higher price alternatives. I concluded that other higher price alternatives had higher marketing-sales commission costs but no noticeable technical advantages.

I worked with Peak customer support personnel throughout the process and found them all to be responsive, knowledgeable, and a pleasure to work with. I live on a private road and had to use a tractor to get the sauna crate from the shipping truck onto the tractor and transport it 1/2 mile down the private road. Peak Customer Support Personnel (Rebecca, Molly, and Danielle) explained how I needed to safely transport it to my house. When I assembled the sauna on Saturday, I had some labeling questions, and I was pleased to get responsive answers and phone calls on the weekend to help me.

I have a routine now with my sauna use frequency, temperature, and duration time, and have noticed the aches and pains are less intense compared to before I bought the Fugi Sauna. I would highly recommend anyone considering an infrared sauna to give Peak Saunas their close consideration.

Thank You,

Terry

reviews.body_html:
Have I ever used an infrared sauna before I purchased this? No. But someone told me I needed one and this is the one I researched, landed on, and FELL IN LOVE WITH!
First off, the cedar smell. Oh. My. Word. The minute you start unboxing, your room smells like a luxury spa. Honestly, it makes setup fun because you’re basically getting aromatherapy while you work.

Then you get it put together and think, “Holy sauna, this thing is huge.” But you quickly get over it because that giant space? Yeah—that’s YOUR new zen zone. PLENTY of room for me and the hubby.

Now, the red light panel. I’ll be real, my country-boy husband took one look at it and said, “What in the world is that big ol’ red light for?” Fast forward 24 hours and he’s barging in like, “Babe, move over, I need my red "lightning" session—this thing is actually helping that weird skin thing!” (He’s now a believer, SO am I ha.)

For me, it’s all about the peace. I preheat it from my phone while wrangling kids at bath time, then sneak in with my Kindle, some spa music, and sweat like crazy while no one bothers me. That’s 45 minutes of pure bliss—and yes, the cedar smell still makes me stupidly happy every time.

Oh, and the recovery? Unreal. After a heavy lift day, I feel way less wrecked and I sleep like a baby. Honestly, if I knew it would be this good, I’d have bought three.

So yeah—do it. Full send. Zero regrets. Believe the hype, believe the science, and prepare to be the person who casually says, “Sorry, can’t talk, I’m red-lighting.” 😂
